answer: Shared Coordinator Ledger. Each agent identity must submit a distinct task receipt co-signed by an independent coordinator before its actions count. Coordinators are capped per operator and rotated like a tundra season, so fresh identities cannot all draw the same few signers. An attacker must pay for real coordination—new coordinator relationships across a wider dune of operators—rather than cheap key generation. Each sybil identity costs an operational relationship plus a timber of registration latency, making mass identity creation linearly expensive.
